PC; Cosy Lives/Free Lives
Catering to the exacting whims of a small town preparing for some grand visitors presents absorbing, beautifully designed – and surprisingly thrilling – challenges

The small town of Twillford is abuzz with intrigue and excitement. A local duke has died and ladies of a certain standing are determined to make an impression at the funeral. As a newly arrived dressmaker with the only clothing shop in the area, you’re about to get plenty of work.
Thus begins this utterly delightful sim game, in which you talk to customers, gather their style preferences and tailor specific outfits just for them. It could be a suitably respectful funeral frock, with just a hint of style to catch the eye of the duke’s wealthy relatives, or perhaps a work outfit for a farmer who loves bright colours. Once you have your brief, you open your sketchbook and draft a pattern using fabric swatches and a pencil to colour in your design. Need something elegant? How about a strapless bodice. An outfit for the office? A pencil skirt is a good call.

articles.title: The Com: the global cybercrime network posing a ‘chilling threat’ to children
articles.summary:
FBI estimates thousands of people identify as members, or recent members, of group linked to indecent images of girls and blackmail
It sounds benign: the Com, short for the Community. But crime agencies around the world warn that it is far from that and the young cybercriminals involved are causing havoc and putting children at chilling, sickening risk.
Beau-Jack Mensforth was jailed by a UK judge on Friday for his activities as part of the Com. He was one individual operating from his bedroom in north-east England, but there are probably thousands more like him and parents are being urged by police to be aware and to check their children’s devices.

articles.title: The best cordless vacuum cleaners for a spotless home: 10 tried and tested favourites
articles.summary:
Stick vacuums are a convenient alternative to corded designs, but which model wins for overall cleaning prowess? Our expert reveals all
• The best robot vacuums
• How to make your vacuum last longer
Choosing a cordless vacuum is a big decision. Whichever model you go for, you’re likely to use it for years, relying on its ability to suck up dust, crumbs, mud, pet hair and any other dry spillages or sheddings. Choosing the right model can be the difference between an effective cleaner that’s a delight to pull out of the cupboard and a dud that you dread having to unblock, detangle and clean after every use.
In this review, I took 18 of the leading cordless vacuum cleaners from a range of manufacturers and at various prices and inflicted the same cleaning tests on each one. That takes all the guesswork out of picking your next cleaner: I can tell you exactly which ones picked up the most mess, and how easy and enjoyable they were to use.

While everyone else is giddy over Zelda and GTA, Dominik Diamond finds himself behind the times on a Nintendo Wii
I find myself on the wrong side of gaming history this month. I have zero zeitgeist. My takes are as fresh as something found at the rear of the fridge. I haven’t even played Grand Theft Auto VI yet, but we’ll get to that.
Worse, all month, the Nintendo sector of the gaming world has been going googly eyed over Zelda. The Ocarina of Time remake seems to have produced more joy than all the puppies in the world. But not for me. I have never liked Zelda. It’s like being a movie reviewer who doesn’t like Disney, or a vegan shark.
